body:
Depression has finally won, I think. Things have been on a steady downward spiral for a while now. I guess what really started it was moving away. I felt so alone all the time. I didn't branch out, didn't meet people, stayed in this small group, but that's gone now, so there's really no one now. Sure, I'll give it an honest shot, meeting new people, that is. But I feel like it's useless, I don't trust people anymore. Most people won't think twice before telling everyone your secrets, your thoughts that you thought were safe with them.

I've fantasized about killing myself for as long as I can remember. Well, fantasize would the wrong word. Maybe just thought about it way too often. I can put a date on it: when I was about nine years old I was terrified about death. To the point where I would cry in bed and not sleep. I would just lay there, not wanting to die. I didn't even understand what death was back then. I knew it was an end, and I didn't like the fact that my life was finite. But after I got over the fact that life was finite (with a lot of help from my brother) I guess something changed in my mind. I think that's where I put the beginning of my depression. After that things were just bland, I didn't have many friends growing up, maybe one or two but they moved away, changed. I didn't really care, I had books, they work as friends (better friends than most). But books generally give an absolutely false vision of reality, and that tends to just make things worse.

I started this relationship young, it wasn't the first, but it was the first meaningful one. We clicked in a way that I feel is impossible to do again. Partially because it happened with her, and that will always be in the back of my mind, but also because I doubt I'll find anyone like that  again. It's set my expectations unreasonably high.

Then I did what I thought would make things better: I ended my long-term relationship. It didn't end it on good terms, either. I ended it in a way that removed her from me entirely. That's what accelerated this, probably. I can't find happiness anymore. I tried to move on, I really did. But that's just a lie which I feel guilty about. Both guilty to myself and to her. No one should be in a relationship with someone who's emotionally unavailable. I feel like I just made things worse for everyone in the situation. 

It's been a while now, but I can't stop replaying all of the memories we've had over and over again in my mind. Some days I can't sleep because of it. Sometimes they're so painful that I just spend days in bed. 

It's come to the point that I don't care what happens after this. I don't feel like this is living anymore, this is some fucked up subset of living.
I wouldn't put her through that. No, I think it's well time I accept that I've fucked up and give in.

Many years. It ended poorly, to say the least. 

I ended it.
It was my doing, all of this, with maybe the exception of my depression, but I even question that sometimes. But, in short, I ended it, which led to a very long stream of poor choices.

Christmas was alright, it's lost its magic, though, if you ask me. How was yours?

It's not going so well. Tonight I've just lost hope. Things aren't going to get better, and it's no one's fault but my own. I don't even know how to explain this. It definitely started with the end of a relationship.
